title: Why Does Your Voice Sound Weird on Recordings?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does your voice sound weird on recordings?
Hear yourself in a video, and it's like a stranger is talking.
When you speak, your voice reaches your ears two ways.
One path goes through the air, out of your mouth and into your ears.
The other goes through your head. Your voice makes your skull vibrate, and that carries sound to your inner ear.
That bone path changes the mix of tones you hear, so your voice sounds fuller to you than on the recording.
A microphone only catches the air path.
So the recording is closer to the voice everyone else hears. The one in your head has an extra path only you get, and that's the one you're used to.
